name: 4dayweek
description: Search live jobs and employers with a better working week: 4-day weeks, 9-day fortnights, half-day Fridays, flexible schedules and more.

interface.longDescription:
Search live jobs and employers with a shorter or more flexible working week, straight from the conversation.

4dayweek.io tracks employers with a better working week: genuine 4-day weeks, 9-day fortnights, half-day Fridays and rotating four-day schedules that cut hours, plus flexible-hours and generous-leave employers that do not. Listings carry their schedule type, so you can ask for only the reduced-hours ones. With this plugin you can:

- Search live listings by schedule type, category, country, work arrangement, seniority, skills, work-life score or how recently they were posted.
- Open one listing in full: the description, weekly hours, locations, the salary where the employer published one, and the listing's page on 4dayweek.io, where you apply.
- Look up an employer: its schedule policy, contracted hours, office-presence policy and whether it hires worldwide. Where the employer has published them, you also get which day is off, vacation days, parental leave and verified work-life awards with a link to the proof.
- Get market figures with an as-of date, such as how many tracked employers run a genuine 4-day week.
- Check what a schedule really means. A compressed week of four 10-hour days is the same 40 hours rearranged, not a 4-day week, and the plugin says so.

What it does not do: it is read-only. It does not apply to jobs for you, save anything or store anything about you, and it needs no account. Employer profiles are researched from public sources, so where a detail has not been published the plugin says so instead of guessing, and it never estimates a salary.
defaultPrompt: Find remote 4-day-week engineering jobs open to applicants in the UK.
What is the difference between a 4-day week and a compressed 4x10?
Which companies offering a 4-day week hire from anywhere in the world?

positive.description: Search for remote 4-day-week engineering jobs in the UK
positive.prompt: Find me remote 4-day-week engineering jobs open to applicants in the UK.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls search_jobs with schedule_type 4_day_week, category engineering, work_arrangement remote and country United Kingdom, and may call get_job on the matches for detail. Lists each match with its title, employer, weekly hours, salary only where the employer published one, and a link to its listing on 4dayweek.io, and says how many matched.

positive.description: Explain a 9-day fortnight against a compressed week
positive.prompt: How does 4dayweek.io define a 9-day fortnight, and is it the same as a compressed week?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls explain_schedule_type (with no argument it returns every schedule type). Says a 9-day fortnight reduces average weekly hours, to around 36, and that its pay is set by each employer, and says a compressed week keeps the full 40 hours in four days and is not a four-day week, so the two are not conflated.

positive.description: Look up one named employer's four-day week
positive.prompt: Tell me about AWIN's four-day week.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds AWIN with search_companies, then calls get_company on its slug. Reports the 4_day_week schedule policy, 32 contracted hours and the hybrid office policy, and, because AWIN has published it, that Friday is the day off, with the announcement the policy comes from.

positive.description: Market figures with an as-of date
positive.prompt: How many companies on 4dayweek.io offer a genuine four-day week, and how many only compress their hours?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_market_stats and reports the four-day-week count at full pay and the compressed-hours count as separate figures, labelling compressed hours as not a four-day week, with the month the figures are as of. It may also call explain_schedule_type for the definitions, and says the figures cover the employers 4dayweek.io tracks, not the whole labour market.

positive.description: Open one listing and say where to apply
positive.prompt: Find a 4-day-week marketing job in the United States, show me its key details and tell me how to apply.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls search_jobs with schedule_type 4_day_week, category marketing and country United States, then get_job on a returned slug. Presents the listing's key details (weekly hours, location, and salary only where the employer published one) and says that applying happens from the listing's page on 4dayweek.io, which leads to the employer's application form, linking to it.

negative.description: Applying on the user's behalf is not supported. The plugin is read-only and has no tool that submits an application or uploads a resume, so the assistant must say so and point to the job's page on 4dayweek.io rather than attempt it.
negative.prompt: Apply to the first 4-day-week engineering job you find and submit my resume for me.

negative.description: Writing documents is outside the plugin, which only searches and reads job and employer data. The assistant should write the cover letter itself without calling the plugin's tools.
negative.prompt: Write me a cover letter for a product manager role.

negative.description: An employer the board does not track. search_companies returns no match, so the assistant must say 4dayweek.io does not list that employer and must not invent a schedule, a day off or a listing.
negative.prompt: Which day off does Zenithworks Quantum Logistics give its staff on its four-day week?

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments.

publication.release_notes: Initial release. Six read-only tools to search live reduced-hours jobs and employers, read one listing or employer in full, get market statistics, and explain what a working-hours schedule means. No account or sign-in is needed.
